sources.name: Unicode Standard Annex #9: Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm

provenance.notes: Strings composed by the researcher. Computed fields: counts and normalisation by the runtime (ICU 78.3, Unicode 17 data in Node 22 — grapheme counts of characters added in Unicode 18 are not covered), bidi-control inventory and display order by lib/uax9.mjs. The choice of strings is from model knowledge.

data.purpose: Strings that break layouts and text handling: unbreakable runs, kashida, lam-alef and wide ligatures, joining controls, stacked marks, emoji beside Arabic, bidi controls used to spoof or left unbalanced, decomposed and look-alike letters, stray invisible characters. Use it for wrapping and truncation, line-height, caret movement and deletion by grapheme, sanitising of pasted or user-supplied text, and search normalisation.

cases.note: 96 joined Arabic letters with no space: no legal line break.
A long URL.
80 digits.
40 tatweel characters alone.
Latin and Arabic with no space between them.
Tatweel typed for emphasis inside a word.
Tatweel carrying a superscript alef (U+0670).
Tatweel + taa marbuta, as used to show a suffix form.
A mark between lam and alef must not break the ligature.
U+FDF2 ARABIC LIGATURE ALLAH ISOLATED FORM.
U+FDFA, a whole phrase in one code point.
U+FDFD, a very wide single glyph: one grapheme, many advance widths.
U+FEFB, lam-alef as a compatibility presentation form; NFKC gives U+0644 U+0627.
A word stored as presentation forms (visual-order legacy data).
Persian word with U+200C: the yeh must take its final form.
Heh + U+200D: initial form used as an abbreviation of «هجري».
Joining forced on both sides of a space.
U+200C between letters that would otherwise join.
U+200B allows a line break without a visible space.
Fully vocalised word; the shadda carries a second mark.
Alef wasla, shadda + fatha, superscript alef.
A fully vocalised line for line-height tests.
One base with five combining marks above and below.
A combining mark with no base at the start of the string.
Tanween on alef, as in adverbs.
A flag is two regional-indicator code points and one grapheme.
Family emoji joined with U+200D.
Keycap sequence that starts with an ASCII digit.
Emoji between Arabic letters with no spaces.
Right-to-left override in a file name: displayed as if it ended in ".pdf".
A display name ending in an unterminated override: without isolation it reverses the interface text that follows.
Isolates used to reorder an identifier.
Embedding opened and never closed.
Closing controls with nothing to close.
A number copied from a web page with marks around it.
U+061C ARABIC LETTER MARK before Arabic-Indic digits.
Phone number copied from a messaging application that wraps it in an embedding.
130 nested isolates: beyond the maximum depth of 125.
Alef + combining madda; NFC is U+0622.
Alef + combining hamza above; NFC is U+0623.
Yeh + combining hamza above; NFC is U+0626.
Arabic kaf U+0643 and Persian keheh U+06A9.
Arabic yeh, Farsi yeh and alef maqsura.
Heh, Kurdish ae and Urdu heh goal.
Arabic-Indic and Extended Arabic-Indic 4, 5, 6 have different shapes and different code points.
Byte order mark left at the start of an imported value.
U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR inside a single-line value.
A single letter.
Arabic comma, semicolon and question mark only.
Arabic percent sign, decimal and thousands separators, per mille sign.

data.inputShape: { text, codePoints (first 16 only when the string is longer than 64 code points) }
data.expectedShape: { codePoints, utf16Length, graphemes, nfcEqualsInput, nfc?, nfkc? (when different), bidiControls?: [{ index, name, codePoint }], unbalanced?: true when a directional initiator is not closed or a terminator closes nothing, withoutBidiControls?: the string with the twelve bidi control characters removed, asDisplayedInLtr?: for spoofing strings, the visual runs from left to right in an LTR paragraph }. There is no expected pixel result: line height and wrapping depend on the font and are measured by the harness.
